_arch_note: exp_n_0083 (untied unembedder, the 1.18923 winner) with ONE change: FFN-slot CompressionMHL lut_tables_per_head 256 -> 128. Everything else held: n_heads=8, nap=7, inner_in_dim=48 (compress ON), inner_out_dim=48 (decompress ON), tie_unembedder=false, forward_mode=hard, depth 6, n_embd 384, n_head 6, seq 512, vocab 32768, 16,000 steps, 24,576 tok/step. FFN LUT table params = n_heads*tph*2^nap*inner_out, so halving tph halves them. PAIRED WITH exp_n_0084 along the heads-vs-tph axis: 0026 is 8 heads x 128 tables = 1024 tables/slot, 0084 is 4 heads x 256 tables = 1024 tables/slot -- the SAME table count reached two different ways, so the pair isolates head-vs-table organization at matched capacity. Anchors: exp_n_0083 1.18923 (untied baseline to preserve), exp_n_0045 1.1977670 (tied baseline), exp_n_0084 (equal-table sibling, not yet run).
_mem_note: device_batch_size 48->24 (grad_accum 1->2) vs exp_n_0045: the untied head materializes the full [tokens,vocab] logits+grad buffer that the tied graph fused away, which OOM'd at bs48 (LUT dense-K [24576,2048,128]~24GB + logits pushed >79GB). Halving the micro-batch keeps effective batch 24,576 identical (grad accumulation is mathematically equivalent) — science unchanged, memory halved.
